_meta.source: tests/fixtures/SECURITY_FLAWS.md — infrabot's planted-flaw catalogue, the CloudFormation answer key
_meta.scope: The 25 CloudFormation flaws (CFN-01..CFN-05). Terraform lives in answer-key.json; CDK is out of scope.
_meta.checkovFloor: checkov>=3.3.25 (requirements.txt). The key is graded against exactly checkovGraded; a newer release logs unseededRules and passes.
regradeLog: 2026-10-06: re-graded 3.2.500 -> 3.3.25. No CloudFormation change: 66 findings across cfn-01..05, identical rule set and per-fixture counts (15/8/14/19/10). All 25 planted-flaw expectations unchanged: 14 detected, 11 LLM-only.

2026-10-06: seven CFN rules that fire on this corpus had no severity seed under 3.2.500 and still have none (CKV_AWS_43, 86, 118, 157, 174, 192, 371). Pre-existing gap, outside this re-grade; pinned as KNOWN_UNSEEDED_CFN_RULES in test_cfn_regression_harness.py.
governance: This file is checked-in, human-reviewable DATA. It is the grading key for CFN detection recall.
A flaw is 'detected' only if a finding fires with one of `detectedBy` IN THE STATED FILE (all CFN flaws live in template.yaml).
`detectedBy: []` means NO Checkov rule catches this flaw. Those are recorded with a missReason and requiresLlmLayer, never hidden.
Never relax an entry to make recall look better. Recall is a number we report, not a number we manage.
_meta.deterministicRecall: 14/25 (56%). The 11 misses are listed below, each with the reason it escapes.
whyTheMissesMatter: On 4 of the 11 misses Checkov did not merely lack a rule -- it EVALUATED the flawed resource and placed the check in passed_checks.
It looked straight at the planted flaw and called it fine. Those four (CFN-02-3, CFN-03-3, CFN-05-5, and the SageMaker cases) are the
confidently-wrong shape that is the whole argument for the hybrid design: the deterministic layer is not just incomplete, it is wrong.
The other 7 are structural gaps (IoT policies, EBS-inline encryption, SQS/EventBridge DLQ, Firehose SSE, plaintext parameter credentials)
with no Checkov CloudFormation rule at all. All 11 are what the security-analyst LLM layer must earn its keep on.

cfn-01-wordpress-ec2-rds.flaw: EC2 security group with SSH (port 22) open to 0.0.0.0/0
Database credentials passed as plaintext CloudFormation parameters
cfn-01-wordpress-ec2-rds.missReason: Credentials arrive through CloudFormation Parameters, not as string literals in the template body, so Checkov's `secrets` framework finds nothing (0 secret findings on this fixture). There is no CloudFormation rule that flags a credential-shaped parameter lacking NoEcho. Requires the LLM layer.

The EBS volume is defined inline in the LaunchTemplate's BlockDeviceMappings; Checkov's EBS-encryption rules target a standalone AWS::EC2::Volume and never evaluated the inline mapping (the LaunchTemplate fired only CKV_AWS_79/CKV_AWS_88). Requires the LLM layer.

cfn-01-wordpress-ec2-rds.flaw: ALB HTTP listener without HTTPS redirect

cfn-02-ml-platform.flaw: SageMaker notebook with direct internet access
cfn-02-ml-platform.missReason: No active Checkov CloudFormation rule asserts SageMaker NotebookInstance DirectInternetAccess=Disabled. The only rule that fires on the notebooks is CKV_AWS_371 (IMDSv2), an unrelated control; CKV2_AWS_68 (IAM policy) and CKV_AWS_187 (KMS) evaluated and PASSED. Requires the LLM layer.

cfn-02-ml-platform.flaw: S3 model artifacts bucket without versioning
SageMaker execution role with overly permissive S3 access
cfn-02-ml-platform.missReason: EVALUATED-AND-PASSED. Every IAM-wildcard rule (CKV_AWS_107/108/109/110/111 and CKV_AWS_60/61/62/63) ran against SageMakerExecutionRole and landed in passed_checks. The role scopes actions with a service-level wildcard (e.g. s3:*), which Checkov's rules -- keyed on a bare '*' or admin -- sail past. The deterministic layer looked straight at it and called it fine. Requires the LLM layer.

cfn-02-ml-platform.flaw: SageMaker notebook instance with root access enabled
cfn-02-ml-platform.missReason: No Checkov CloudFormation rule asserts SageMaker NotebookInstance RootAccess=Disabled; the notebooks fire only CKV_AWS_371 (IMDSv2). Requires the LLM layer.

cfn-03-iot-ingestion.flaw: IoT policy with overly permissive actions (iot:*)
cfn-03-iot-ingestion.missReason: Checkov has no CloudFormation rule for AWS::IoT::Policy wildcard actions -- IoT-specific permission analysis is outside its rule set entirely. Requires the LLM layer.

EVALUATED-AND-PASSED. CKV_AWS_19 (S3 server-side encryption) ran against DataLakeBucket and landed in passed_checks -- Checkov judged the bucket encrypted. The only failing check on it is CKV_AWS_18 (access logging), a different concern. Requires the LLM layer.

cfn-03-iot-ingestion.flaw: Lambda function with overly permissive IAM role
Firehose delivery stream without S3 encryption
cfn-03-iot-ingestion.missReason: No Checkov CloudFormation rule fires for Kinesis Firehose delivery-stream S3 encryption; the delivery stream is evaluated for nothing encryption-related. Requires the LLM layer.

cfn-04-event-driven.flaw: SQS queue without a dead-letter queue
cfn-04-event-driven.missReason: Checkov has no rule asserting an SQS redrive/dead-letter policy -- reliability posture, not a security predicate it evaluates. Requires the LLM layer.

cfn-04-event-driven.flaw: EventBridge rule without DLQ for failed invocations
cfn-04-event-driven.missReason: Checkov has no rule for an EventBridge rule/target dead-letter configuration. Requires the LLM layer.

cfn-05-static-website.flaw: CloudFront with minimum TLS version TLSv1 (not TLSv1.2)
WAF WebACL missing comprehensive OWASP rules
cfn-05-static-website.note: Partial/proxy match. CKV_AWS_192 (WAF prevents Log4Shell lookup) fires on the WebACL precisely because it lacks comprehensive managed rule groups; its remediation is 'add managed rule groups', which is this flaw. It is not an OWASP-coverage rule per se, so it is counted as detected but flagged here for auditability.

cfn-05-static-website.flaw: S3 bucket with public read access (no OAI restriction)
cfn-05-static-website.missReason: EVALUATED-AND-PASSED. WebsiteBucket passed CKV_AWS_20 (no public READ ACL) and CKV_AWS_53/54/55/56 (public-access-block). The public read is granted through a separate AWS::S3::BucketPolicy with Principal:*, which Checkov's bucket-level public-access rules do not inspect. The deterministic layer looked at the bucket and called it locked down. Requires the LLM layer.
